newsitem.title: UK: UK fund manager Henderson cuts notice period.
newsitem.headline: UK fund manager Henderson cuts notice period.

text.p: UK independent fund manager Henderson Investors said on Friday it had cut the notice period on its management contracts with investment trusts to one year from two.
In effect, analysts said, Henderson has shortened its own leash, making it easier for investment trust boards to switch managers or wind down funds if performance is poor.
"We are setting a new standard, confident in our ability to perform," said James de Sausmarez, group personal investors director at Henderson.

"Fund management requires a long-term commitment in terms of setting up resources, so it is a matter of striking a fair balance which recognises this commitment, but at the same time does not impose inappropriate constraints on the trusts."
Until now, Henderson, Britain's largest independent fund manager with 5 billion sterling in 21 investment trusts, has operated under two-year rolling contracts.

"We applaud this sort of move," said Charles Cade, an investment trust analyst at Merrill Lynch. "It makes it easier for poorer performing trusts to return assets to shareholders. It cuts a layer of cost," he said.
Many UK investment trusts have seen their share prices experience widening discounts to asset value in the past year, Cade said, making more wind-downs a possibility.
